questions.q: With reference to the National Commission to Review the Working of the Constitution (NCRWC), consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It was set up by an Act of Parliament in the year 2000. 2️⃣ It was an 11-member commission headed by M.N. Venkatachaliah, a former Chief Justice of India. 3️⃣ The commission submitted its final report in the year 2002.
questions.e: The NCRWC was set up by a resolution of the Government of India in 2000, not by an Act of Parliament. It consisted of 11 members under the chairmanship of M.N. Venkatachaliah and submitted its report in 2002.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the 'Terms of Reference' provided to the National Commission to Review the Working of the Constitution?
o: The commission was tasked with rewriting the Constitution to suit modern needs.
The commission's recommendations were mandatory and binding on the Parliament.
The commission had the authority to alter the 'basic structure' of the Constitution.
The commission was required to recommend changes within the framework of parliamentary democracy.
questions.e: The terms of reference specified that recommendations must be made within the framework of parliamentary democracy and without interfering with the 'basic structure'. The commission clarified its role was to review, not rewrite, and its nature was only advisory.

questions.q: Consider the following individuals who were members of the National Commission to Review the Working of the Constitution: 1️⃣ Soli Sorabjee 2️⃣ P.A. Sangma 3️⃣ R.S. Sarkaria 4️⃣ Abid Hussain. How many of the above were members of the commission?
questions.e: The commission included several notable figures: Soli Sorabjee (Attorney-General), P.A. Sangma (former Speaker of Lok Sabha), R.S. Sarkaria (former SC judge), and Abid Hussain (former Ambassador). P.A. Sangma resigned three months before the report submission.

questions.q: The National Commission to Review the Working of the Constitution identified eleven areas of study. Which of the following was NOT among those identified areas?
o: Strengthening the institutions of parliamentary democracy.
Redefining the boundaries of Indian States.
Decentralization and empowerment of Panchayati Raj Institutions.
Electoral reforms and standards in political life.
questions.e: The commission identified eleven areas on its own, including parliamentary democracy, electoral reforms, socio-economic change, Union-State relations, and decentralization. Redefining state boundaries was not listed as one of these eleven specific study areas.

questions.q: Regarding the 'Areas of Concern' identified by the NCRWC, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The commission noted a fundamental breach of constitutional faith by Governments. 2️⃣ It observed that public servants often forget they are meant to serve the people. 3️⃣ It stated that the dignity of the individual has remained a fully redeemed pledge in modern India.
questions.e: The commission perceived a loss of faith in governance and noted that public servants are not always alive to their role as servants of the people. However, it explicitly stated that the dignity of the individual has remained an "unredeemed pledge".

questions.q: Which of the following statements regarding the 'criminalization of politics' was highlighted as a concern by the NCRWC?
o: The politician-criminal-bureaucratic nexus has reached unprecedented levels.
Criminalization of politics is a minor issue compared to fiscal deficits.
Political activity in India is characterized by pervasive purity.
The electoral system is highly efficient at preventing criminals from entering law-making institutions.
questions.e: The commission expressed grave concern over the pervasive impurity of the political climate, stating that the politician-criminal-bureaucratic nexus requires strong systemic changes. It also noted the electoral system's inability to prevent the entry of criminals.

questions.q: With reference to political instability mentioned in the NCRWC report, consider the following: 1️⃣ Between 1989 and 2002, the country saw five General Elections to the Lok Sabha. 2️⃣ Political instability has high economic and administrative costs. 3️⃣ Only two Prime Ministers ruled India for the first 54 years of independence.
questions.e: The report mentions that from 1989 onwards, there were five General Elections to the Lok Sabha, contributing to colossal costs. It also notes that four (not two) Prime Ministers ruled for 40 years out of the first 54 years of independence.

questions.q: According to the NCRWC, which of the following is a disturbing reality of the Indian economy?
o: Legitimate governments find it very easy to confront parallel governments.
The economy is gradually moving away from a debt-trap.
The society is being pushed into extra-legal systems and crime-syndicates due to fiscal policies and corruption.
The economy is entirely free from the influence of black money.
questions.e: The commission stated the economy is sinking into a debt-trap and that corruption and wasteful expenditure are pushing society toward crime-syndicates and mob-rule. It warned that illegal outfits might eventually dictate terms to legitimate governments.

questions.q: Which of the following was identified as an area of concern regarding the 'Administration of Justice' by the NCRWC?
o: The costs of litigation and delays in law have become proverbial.
There is an adequate institutional arrangement for witness protection in sensitive trials.
The criminal justice system is functioning at its peak efficiency.
The quality of investigations and prosecutions requires no further review.
questions.e: The commission noted that the criminal justice system is on the verge of collapse. It highlighted that law's delay and litigation costs are proverbial and called for better arrangements for victim and witness protection.

questions.q: In its final report, the National Commission to Review the Working of the Constitution made a total of 249 recommendations. How were these recommendations categorized regarding their implementation?
o: 200 involved legislative measures and 49 involved constitutional amendments.
100 involved constitutional amendments and 149 involved executive action.
58 involved constitutional amendments, 86 involved legislative measures, and 105 involved executive action.
questions.e: Out of the 249 total recommendations, the commission specified that 58 would require amending the Constitution, 86 would need new laws (legislative), and 105 could be done through government orders (executive).

questions.q: Regarding recommendations on Fundamental Rights, the NCRWC suggested extending the scope of prohibition against discrimination (Articles 15 and 16) to include which of the following?
o: Ethnic or social origin, political or other opinion, property or birth
questions.e: The commission recommended that the grounds for non-discrimination in Articles 15 and 16 be broadened to include ethnic or social origin, political or other opinion, property, or birth.

questions.q: Which of the following new Fundamental Rights were recommended by the NCRWC? 1️⃣ Right against torture and inhuman treatment. 2️⃣ Right to privacy and family life. 3️⃣ Right to safe drinking water and sustainable development. 4️⃣ Right to travel to Mars.
questions.e: The NCRWC proposed several new rights, including protection against torture, the right to privacy, and the right to safe drinking water and ecology. It did not include a right to travel to Mars.

questions.q: What change did the NCRWC recommend for the Right to Education (Article 21-A)?
o: It should be moved from Fundamental Rights to Directive Principles.
It should only be available to children of tax-paying citizens.
Free education should only be provided up to the age of 10.
It should be enlarged to complete the age of 18 years for girls and members of SCs and STs.
questions.e: The commission recommended enlarging the right to education to provide free education for all children until 14, and specifically until 18 for girls and members of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

questions.q: Concerning preventive detention (Article 22), the NCRWC recommended that the maximum period of such detention should be:
questions.e: The commission proposed two specific changes for Article 22: reducing the maximum period of preventive detention to six months and requiring the advisory board to consist of serving High Court judges.

questions.q: Which religious groups did the NCRWC recommend should be treated as religions separate from Hinduism under Article 25?
questions.e: The commission recommended that Sikhism, Jainism, and Buddhism be treated as distinct religions and that the existing provisions grouping them under the definition of 'Hindu' be deleted.

questions.q: Regarding the 'Right to Property' (Article 300-A), the NCRWC recommended:
o: Moving it back to the list of Fundamental Rights.
Suitable rehabilitation for SCs and STs if their land is acquired.
Compensation at ten times the market rate for all citizens.
questions.e: The commission recommended recasting Article 300-A to ensure no arbitrary deprivation and specifically to provide a right to "suitable rehabilitation" for SCs and STs when their agricultural or forest land is acquired.

questions.q: Which of the following was a recommendation by the NCRWC regarding the Directive Principles of State Policy?
o: The heading of Part-IV should be 'Directive Principles of State Policy and Action'.
Population control should be removed from the state's agenda.
The Directive Principles should be abolished to focus on Fundamental Rights.
They should be made legally enforceable in courts.
questions.e: The commission suggested renaming Part-IV to include "Action" and recommended adding a new Directive Principle on population control.

questions.q: With reference to Fundamental Duties (Article 51-A), which of the following new duties was suggested by the NCRWC?
o: Duty to serve in the military for two years.
Duty to report all neighbors to the police.
Duty to vote at elections and pay taxes.
Duty to plant at least ten trees every year.
questions.e: New fundamental duties proposed included the duty to vote, participate in democratic governance, pay taxes, and foster family values and responsible parenthood.

questions.q: What did the NCRWC recommend regarding the immunity of legislators under Article 105?
o: Immunity should only apply to the Prime Minister.
Legislators should have no immunity at all.
Immunity should not cover corrupt acts committed in connection with duties in the House.
Immunity should be absolute and cover all acts.
questions.e: The commission recommended amending Article 105 (and 194 for states) to clarify that parliamentary privileges do not protect members from legal action for corrupt acts.

questions.q: For a motion of no-confidence to be brought against the government, the NCRWC recommended that what percentage of the House members should give notice?
questions.e: To prevent frequent or frivolous motions, the commission recommended that at least 20 per cent of the total membership of the House must give notice for a no-confidence motion.

questions.q: Which of the following is the 'system of constructive vote of no confidence' as recommended by the NCRWC?
o: A vote that only criticizes the government without removing it.
A motion of no-confidence that must be accompanied by a proposal for an alternative leader.
A vote where only the opposition is allowed to speak.
A requirement that the government resigns only if 75% of members vote against it.
questions.e: The commission proposed the 'constructive vote of no confidence', meaning a no-confidence motion against a Prime Minister must simultaneously name and vote for a replacement leader.

questions.q: The NCRWC recommended a ceiling on the number of Ministers in any State or the Union government. What was this recommended limit?
o: 25 ministers regardless of the size of the house.
5 per cent of the total strength of the house.
15 per cent of the total strength of the house.
10 per cent of the total strength of the popular house.
questions.e: To prevent oversized cabinets, the commission suggested a legal ceiling of 10 per cent of the strength of the Lok Sabha or State Legislative Assembly for the Council of Ministers.

questions.q: Regarding the appointment of the Governor of a state, what did the NCRWC recommend?
o: The Governor should be elected by the people of the state.
The Governor should always be a retired general.
The post of Governor should be abolished.
The President should consult the Chief Minister of that state before appointment.
questions.e: The commission recommended that the President should appoint a state's Governor only after consulting with the Chief Minister of that particular state.

questions.q: What was the NCRWC's recommendation regarding Article 356 (President's Rule)?
o: It should be used as a remedy of the last resort and tested on the floor of the House.
The President should be able to impose it without any conditions.
It should only be used during a declared war.
It should be completely deleted from the Constitution.
questions.e: The commission advised that Article 356 should not be deleted but used sparingly as a last resort. It also emphasized that whether a ministry has lost confidence must be tested on the floor of the House.

questions.q: To handle river water disputes, the NCRWC suggested they should be heard by a bench of the Supreme Court consisting of:
o: The Chief Justice of India alone
questions.e: The commission recommended that river water disputes between States/Centre should be heard by a Supreme Court bench of at least three judges, or five if necessary for final disposal.

questions.q: Regarding the 'Judiciary', which of the following was a recommendation of the NCRWC?
o: The retirement age of High Court judges should be reduced to 60.
A National Judicial Commission should be established to recommend SC judge appointments.
District courts should have the power to declare Acts of Parliament unconstitutional.
All courts should have the power to punish for contempt of itself.
questions.e: The commission proposed a National Judicial Commission for appointments and recommended increasing the retirement age of HC judges to 65 and SC judges to 68. It also suggested limiting the power to declare laws unconstitutional to only the SC and HCs.

questions.q: Which of the following recommendations was made by the NCRWC regarding the Fifth and Sixth Schedules?
o: Only urban areas should be covered under the Sixth Schedule.
All tribal areas under the Sixth Schedule should be moved to the Fifth Schedule.
All tribal areas under the Fifth Schedule should be transferred to the Sixth Schedule.
questions.e: The commission recommended that tribal areas currently governed by the Fifth Schedule should be transferred to the Sixth Schedule to improve the pace of socio-economic development.

questions.q: Concerning 'Decentralization', the NCRWC recommended that the Election Commission of India (ECI) should have the power to:
o: Audit the accounts of the Prime Minister.
Issue directions to the State Election Commission.
questions.e: The commission proposed that the ECI should be empowered to give directions to State Election Commissions and that State Election Commissions should submit reports to the ECI and the Governor.

questions.q: In the context of electoral processes, what did the NCRWC suggest regarding candidates contesting from multiple constituencies?
o: Candidates should be encouraged to contest from at least three seats.
Candidates should not be allowed to contest simultaneously from more than one constituency.
There should be no limit on the number of seats a candidate can contest.
Only independent candidates can contest from two seats.
questions.e: The commission recommended that a candidate should be restricted to contesting for a single office from only one constituency at a time.

questions.q: What was the NCRWC's recommendation regarding the 'None of the Above' (NOTA) or negative voting option?
o: The commission proposed that NOTA voters should be fined.
The commission suggested that negative votes should be counted as double.
The commission recommended against such a system.
The commission recommended examining the system of 50 per cent plus one vote polled.
questions.e: While the document discusses NOTA in the context of the PUCL case, the NCRWC specifically recommended that the government and ECI should examine the "run-off contest" system where a representative must win 50% plus one vote.

questions.q: Regarding political parties, the NCRWC recommended that a candidate should be disqualified if:
o: They were convicted of a criminal offence or charges have been framed by a court.
They belong to a small political party.
questions.e: The commission proposed a law requiring parties to deny tickets to any candidate convicted of a crime or against whom a court has framed criminal charges.

questions.q: What did the NCRWC recommend for the Anti-Defection Law (Tenth Schedule)?
o: The Speaker should have the final and unchallengeable power to decide on defection.
It should be abolished to allow freedom of speech.
All persons defecting must resign and contest fresh elections.
Defectors should be allowed to become ministers immediately.
questions.e: The commission recommended that any defector (individual or group) must resign and seek re-election. It also suggested that the power to decide on disqualification should shift from the Speaker to the Election Commission.

questions.q: In the *Romesh Thappar case (1950)*, the Supreme Court ruled that the freedom of speech and expression includes:
o: The right to remain silent during police questioning.
The right to strike in essential services.
The freedom of circulation of ideas.
questions.e: The Court held that Article 19(1)(a) includes the freedom of propagation of ideas, which is ensured by the freedom of circulation. It declared the Madras government's ban on the journal 'Cross Roads' void.

questions.q: What was the immediate 'Impact of the Judgement' in the *Romesh Thappar case (1950)*?
o: The Supreme Court was abolished for two years.
It led to the 42nd Amendment Act.
The 1st Amendment Act added "public order" as a reasonable restriction in Article 19(2).
questions.e: As a sequel to the judgement where the court refused to allow restrictions on the ground of public order (since it wasn't in the original text), the 1st Amendment Act of 1951 added "public order" as a valid ground for restricting free speech.

questions.q: In the *A.K. Gopalan case (1950)*, the Supreme Court's interpretation of 'personal liberty' under Article 21 was:
o: A protection against both the executive and the legislature.
Broad and inclusive of all human rights.
Narrow and meant only liberty of the physical body.
Identical to the American 'due process of law'.
questions.e: The court took a narrow, 'textualist' approach, ruling that 'personal liberty' meant freedom from physical restraint and that Article 21 protected citizens only against arbitrary executive action, not legislative action.

questions.q: The *Champakam Dorairajan case (1951)* led to which of the following constitutional changes?
o: Granting of the right to vote to women.
Insertion of Clause (4) in Article 15 by the 1st Amendment Act.
questions.e: After the Court struck down communal reservations in medical colleges, the 1st Amendment was enacted to add Article 15(4), allowing the state to make special provisions for backward classes, SCs, and STs.

questions.q: In the *Shankari Prasad case (1951)*, the Supreme Court held that:
o: Parliament's power to amend the Constitution under Article 368 includes the power to amend Fundamental Rights.
The Preamble is the most important part of the Constitution.
questions.e: The court ruled that Article 368 gives Parliament the power to amend any part of the Constitution, including Part III, and that a constitutional amendment is not a 'law' subject to the restrictions of Article 13(2).

questions.q: What was the Supreme Court's ruling regarding the Preamble in the *Berubari Union case (1960)*?
o: The Preamble was written by the British Parliament.
The Preamble is the only part of the Constitution that cannot be amended.
The Preamble is the 'Basic Structure' of the Constitution.
The Preamble is NOT a part of the Constitution.
questions.e: In this case, which dealt with the cession of Indian territory to Pakistan, the Supreme Court explicitly held that the Preamble is not a part of the Constitution.

questions.q: The *K.M. Nanavati case (1961)* is significant in Indian legal history primarily because it led to:
o: The abolition of the Jury System of trial.
The introduction of the death penalty.
questions.e: This case exposed the shortcomings of the Jury System. While some trials continued for a short while after, the 1973 Code of Criminal Procedure eventually removed the system of trial by jury in India completely.

questions.q: In the *I.C. Golak Nath case (1967)*, the Supreme Court ruled that:
o: The amending power under Article 368 cannot be used to take away Fundamental Rights.
The Parliament is supreme over the Constitution.
questions.e: Overruling earlier verdicts, the Court held that Fundamental Rights are "transcendental and immutable" and cannot be abridged by constitutional amendments. It applied the doctrine of "prospective overruling".

questions.q: Which amendment was enacted specifically to override the judgement in the *I.C. Golak Nath case*?
questions.e: The 24th Amendment Act was passed to clarify that Parliament has the power to amend any part of the Constitution, including Fundamental Rights, and that such amendments are not 'laws' under Article 13.

questions.q: The 'Doctrine of Basic Structure' was propounded by the Supreme Court in which landmark case?
questions.e: In the Kesavananda Bharati case, the Court ruled that while Parliament can amend any part of the Constitution, it cannot alter its "basic structure" or "basic features".

questions.q: What was the significance of the *Indira Nehru Gandhi case (1975)*?
o: It reaffirmed the doctrine of basic structure by striking down Article 329A (clause 4).
It declared that only the President can decide election disputes.
It abolished the post of Prime Minister.
It held that Fundamental Rights are not part of the basic structure.
questions.e: The Court struck down a provision that kept election disputes of the Prime Minister and Speaker outside judicial purview, stating it violated the basic structure of the Constitution.

questions.q: Which case is popularly known as the 'Habeas Corpus case'?
questions.e: The A.D.M. Jabalpur vs. Shivakant Shukla case is known as the Habeas Corpus case. In this flawed 1976 judgement, the Court held that the right to life could be suspended during an emergency.

questions.q: The *Maneka Gandhi case (1978)* is famous for introducing which concept into Indian judicial interpretation?
o: American concept of 'due process of law'
Right to Property as a Fundamental Right
questions.e: The Court overruled the A.K. Gopalan case, holding that 'procedure established by law' must be just, fair, and reasonable, effectively introducing 'due process' and the 'golden triangle' of Articles 14, 19, and 21.

questions.q: In the *Bachan Singh case (1980)*, the Supreme Court laid down the doctrine of:
questions.e: The Court upheld the death penalty but ruled that it should be an exception and awarded only in the "rarest of rare cases" where the alternative option is unquestionably foreclosed.

questions.q: The *Minerva Mills case (1980)* is important because it:
o: Held that Directive Principles always override Fundamental Rights.
Struck down Clauses (4) and (5) of Article 368, restoring the balance between FRs and DPSPs.
Abolished judicial review for all constitutional amendments.
Gave the Parliament unlimited power to amend the Constitution.
questions.e: The Court invalidated amendments that gave Parliament unlimited power, holding that the limited amending power of Parliament and the harmony between FRs and DPSPs are basic features of the Constitution.

questions.q: What did the Supreme Court rule in the *Shah Bano case (1985)* regarding Section 125 of the CrPC?
o: It is secular in character and applies to all religions, including Muslims.
It only applies to women who have not received 'Mahr'.
It is unconstitutional because it interferes with personal laws.
questions.e: The Court held that a Muslim husband must pay maintenance to a divorced wife beyond the 'iddat' period and that Section 125 of the CrPC prevails over personal law in case of conflict.

questions.q: The *D.C. Wadhwa case (1986)* dealt with the misuse of which power by the Governor?
o: Power to appoint the Chief Minister.
questions.e: The Court struck down the practice of re-promulgating ordinances without placing them before the legislature, calling it a "fraud on the Constitution" and a subversion of the democratic process.

questions.q: Which principle was introduced by the Supreme Court in the *M.C. Mehta case (1986)*, also known as the Oleum Gas Leak case?
questions.e: The Court introduced the principle of "absolute liability" (no-fault liability) for enterprises engaged in hazardous activities, replacing the older, more limited "strict liability" rule.

questions.q: In the *Indra Sawhney case (1992)*, the Supreme Court:
o: Upheld 27% reservation for OBCs subject to the exclusion of the 'creamy layer'.
Allowed 10% additional reservation for economically backward sections of higher castes.
Struck down all reservations for OBCs.
Ruled that total reservation can exceed 75%.
questions.e: The Court upheld 27% OBC reservation in government jobs but insisted on the 'creamy layer' exclusion and a 50% overall cap on reservations.

questions.q: The *Mohini Jain (1992)* and *Unni Krishnan (1993)* cases primarily dealt with which right?
questions.e: These cases established that the Right to Education is a fundamental right flowing from Article 21. This eventually led to the 86th Amendment Act and the insertion of Article 21A.

questions.q: The "collegium system" for the appointment of judges was invented following which landmark judgement?
questions.e: In the Second Judges case (Supreme Court Advocates-on-Record Association vs. Union of India), the Court interpreted 'consultation' as 'concurrence', leading to the birth of the collegium system.

questions.q: In the *S.R. Bommai case (1994)*, the Supreme Court held that:
o: The President's proclamation under Article 356 is not subject to judicial review.
The Governor can dismiss a ministry at any time.
Secularism is a part of the basic structure of the Constitution.
State Assemblies can be dissolved before Parliament approves the proclamation.
questions.e: The Court ruled that Article 356 is subject to judicial review and that the assembly should not be dissolved until Parliament approves the proclamation. It also affirmed secularism as a basic feature.

questions.q: The 'Vishaka Guidelines' were laid down by the Supreme Court to address:
o: Sexual harassment of women at the workplace.
questions.e: In the absence of a domestic law, the Court issued guidelines to prevent sexual harassment at workplaces, which remained in force until the 2013 Act was passed.

questions.q: In the *Vineet Narain case (1997)*, the Supreme Court issued directions to:
o: Allow ministers to supervise all CBI investigations.
Make the ED a private organization.
Confer statutory status on the Central Vigilance Commission (CVC).
questions.e: The Court directed that the CVC be given statutory status and the CBI be made an autonomous body to function without political interference.

questions.q: According to the *Association for Democratic Reforms case (2002)*, voters have a right to know which of the following about a candidate?
o: The names of all their childhood friends.
Their criminal antecedents, assets, liabilities, and educational qualifications.
questions.e: The Court held that a voter's right to know the background of a candidate is part of the freedom of speech and expression under Article 19(1)(a).

questions.q: In the *T.M.A. Pai Foundation case (2002)*, the Supreme Court ruled that for determining 'minority' status under Article 30:
o: The whole of India is the unit.
Only religion, not language, is a criteria.
questions.e: The Court held that since states were reorganized on linguistic lines, the 'unit' for determining both religious and linguistic minorities must be the State.

questions.q: The *Naveen Jindal case (2004)* established that the right to fly the national flag with dignity is:
questions.e: The Supreme Court held that flying the national flag is an expression of allegiance and pride, falling under the freedom of speech and expression.

questions.q: Which case is associated with 'Police Reforms' and the setting up of a State Security Commission?
questions.e: In the Prakash Singh case, the SC issued seven directives to ensure police function without political interference, including the creation of a State Security Commission and a minimum tenure for the DGP.

questions.q: In the *I.R. Coelho case (2007)*, the Supreme Court ruled that laws placed in the Ninth Schedule:
o: Can be challenged if they violate the 'Basic Structure' of the Constitution after April 24, 1973.
Must be removed every five years.
Are completely immune to judicial review.
questions.e: Reaffirming the Waman Rao case, the Court held that any law added to the Ninth Schedule after the Kesavananda Bharati verdict date is open to challenge on basic structure grounds.

questions.q: The *Aruna Ramachandra Shanbaug case (2011)* made which of the following permissible in India under strict conditions?
questions.e: The Court held that while active euthanasia remains illegal, passive euthanasia (withdrawing life support) is permissible subject to approval by the High Court and a medical board.

questions.q: Which case led to the introduction of the "None of the Above" (NOTA) option in EVMs?
o: People's Union for Civil Liberties (PUCL) case (2013)
questions.e: The SC directed the ECI to provide a NOTA button so voters could exercise their right not to vote while maintaining secrecy, linking it to the freedom of expression.

questions.q: In the *Lily Thomas case (2013)*, the Supreme Court ruled that:
o: A legislator must be convicted for at least 10 years to be disqualified.
Only the President can disqualify a member of Parliament.
Convicted legislators lose their membership of the House immediately upon conviction.
Convicted legislators can continue in office if they file an appeal.
questions.e: The Court struck down Section 8(4) of the RPA 1951, which previously gave convicted members three months to appeal before being disqualified.

questions.q: The *National Legal Services Authority (NALSA) case (2014)* is landmark for:
o: Legalizing child marriage in some states.
Recognizing Transgender persons as 'third gender' with fundamental rights.
Granting the right to vote to foreigners.
questions.e: The Court upheld the rights of transgender persons to self-identify their gender and directed the government to treat them as socially and educationally backward classes for reservations.

questions.q: In the *Shreya Singhal case (2015)*, the Supreme Court struck down Section 66A of the IT Act because:
o: It only applied to people using laptops.
It was not being used by the police.
It was vague and violated the freedom of speech and expression.
It allowed the government to read all private emails.
questions.e: The Court held that Section 66A was unconstitutional as it created a vague offence that was not saved by the reasonable restrictions under Article 19(2).

questions.q: The 99th Amendment Act and the National Judicial Appointments Commission (NJAC) Act were declared unconstitutional in which case?
questions.e: The Supreme Court (in the Advocates-on-Record Association case) held that the NJAC affected the independence of the judiciary, which is a part of the basic structure.

questions.q: In the *Shayara Bano case (2017)*, what was declared unconstitutional by the Supreme Court?
questions.e: The Court held that instant triple talaq is arbitrary, violates Article 14, and is not a fundamental part of Islamic theology.

questions.q: The *K.S. Puttaswamy case (2017)* is most famous for declaring which of the following as a Fundamental Right?
questions.e: A nine-judge bench unanimously declared that the right to privacy is protected as an intrinsic part of the right to life and personal liberty under Article 21.

questions.q: With reference to the *Indian Young Lawyers Association case (2018)*, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It is popularly known as the Sabarimala case. 2️⃣ The Court held that the ban on women of age group 10-50 violates Articles 14, 21, and 25. 3️⃣ The judgement was unanimously accepted and implemented without any protests.
questions.e: While the Court struck down the ban on women's entry as unconstitutional, the judgement led to massive protests in Kerala. Later, the case was referred to a larger bench for review.

questions.q: Adultery was decriminalized in India by the Supreme Court in which of the following cases?
o: Joseph Shine vs. Union of India (2018)
M. Siddiq vs. Mahant Suresh Das (2019)
Shayara Bano vs. Union of India (2017)
Navtej Singh Johar vs. Union of India (2018)
questions.e: The Court struck down Section 497 of the IPC, ruling that it treated women as property of their husbands and violated Articles 14, 15, and 21.

questions.q: In the *Navtej Singh Johar case (2018)*, the Supreme Court:
o: Decriminalized homosexuality by partly striking down Section 377 of the IPC.
Banned the LGBT community from participating in politics.
questions.e: The Court held that Section 377 was unconstitutional in so far as it criminalized consensual sexual acts between adults of the same sex.

questions.q: Regarding the *M. Siddiq case (2019)* (Ayodhya case), which of the following is true?
o: The entire disputed land was awarded to the deity Ram Lalla Virajman.
The land was divided equally between three parties.
The Supreme Court refused to hear the case, calling it a political issue.
The Babri Masjid was ordered to be rebuilt at the same spot.
questions.e: The Court awarded the 2.77 acres of disputed land to the Hindu side and directed the government to provide an alternative 5 acres of land to the Muslim side for a mosque.

questions.q: Which of the following cases established that the freedom of speech and expression over the internet enjoys constitutional protection?
o: Internet and Mobile Association of India case
questions.e: Dealing with the internet shutdown in J&K, the Court held that access to the internet is a medium for exercising the fundamental rights under Article 19(1)(a) and 19(1)(g).

questions.q: The ban on cryptocurrency trading by the RBI was struck down by the Supreme Court in 2020 based on the ground of:
questions.e: The Court declared the RBI circular illegal because it was a disproportionate restriction, as the RBI had not found that banks suffered any actual loss from virtual currency exchanges.

questions.q: Match the following rights declared as part of Article 21 with their respective cases: 1️⃣ Right to speedy trial - Hussainara Khatoon 2️⃣ Right to travel abroad - Satwant Singh Sawhney 3️⃣ Right to sleep - Ramlila Maidan Incident 4️⃣ Right to shelter - Shantistar Builders. How many pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: The Supreme Court has expanded Article 21 to include numerous rights: speedy trial (Hussainara Khatoon), travel abroad (Satwant Singh Sawhney), sleep (Ramlila Maidan), and shelter (Shantistar Builders).

questions.q: Which of the following amendments was declared UNCONSTITUTIONAL (in total) by the Supreme Court?
questions.e: The 99th Amendment Act, which sought to establish the National Judicial Appointments Commission (NJAC), was struck down in its entirety in 2015.

questions.q: The *Hussainara Khatoon case (1979)* is significant for establishing which right as an integral part of Article 21?
questions.e: This case is a landmark in Indian legal history for recognizing that a speedy trial is a fundamental right of every accused person.

questions.q: Which case is popularly known as the 'Pavement Dwellers case'?
o: Bandhua Mukti Morcha vs. Union of India
Olga Tellis vs. Bombay Municipal Corporation
Sheela Barse vs. State of Maharashtra
Olga Tellis vs. State of Bihar
questions.e: The Olga Tellis case of 1985 is known as the Pavement Dwellers case, where the Court recognized the Right to Livelihood as a part of the Right to Life.

questions.q: The "Right against the adverse effects of climate change" was declared as an integral part of Article 21 in which recent case (2024)?
o: M.K. Ranjitsinh vs. Union of India
Anuradha Bhasin vs. Union of India
Rambabu Singh Thakur vs. Sunil Arora
M. Siddiq vs. Mahant Suresh Das
questions.e: In a significant expansion of environmental jurisprudence in 2024, the Supreme Court recognized the right against climate change's adverse effects under Article 21.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding the *Lily Thomas case (2013)*: 1️⃣ It struck down Section 8(4) of the RPA, 1951. 2️⃣ It allowed convicted members a 3-month grace period to appeal. 3️⃣ The judgement led to the immediate disqualification of several members of Parliament.
questions.e: The judgement explicitly struck down the 3-month grace period (Section 8(4)) as unconstitutional, leading to immediate disqualification upon conviction.

questions.q: The 'Right to die with dignity' (Passive Euthanasia) was reaffirmed as a part of Article 21 in which case following Aruna Shanbaug?
o: Joseph Shine vs. Union of India
K.S. Puttaswamy vs. Union of India
Navtej Singh Johar vs. Union of India
Common Cause (A Regd. Society) vs. Union of India (2018)
questions.e: In 2018, the Supreme Court in the Common Cause case reaffirmed that the right to die with dignity is a fundamental right, specifically allowing for passive euthanasia.

questions.q: Regarding the *Rambabu Singh Thakur case (2020)*, political parties are required to:
o: Pay a fine for every candidate with a criminal record.
Select only those candidates who have never been to court.
Upload detailed information about candidates with criminal antecedents on their websites.
questions.e: The SC made it mandatory for parties to publish criminal records of candidates, the nature of offences, and reasons why someone without a criminal record was not selected.

questions.q: Which case led to the enactment of the *Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019*?
o: Navtej Singh Johar vs. Union of India
Shreya Singhal vs. Union of India
questions.e: The 2014 NALSA judgement provided the legal foundation for the protection of transgender rights, eventually resulting in the 2019 legislation.

questions.q: The Supreme Court in the *Anuradha Bhasin case* ruled that suspension of internet services:
o: Can only be done by the President of India.
Cannot be ordered indefinitely and must adhere to proportionality.
Does not fall under the purview of judicial review.
Is always illegal under any circumstance.
questions.e: The Court ruled that an indefinite suspension of internet is impermissible and that any shutdown must be temporary and subject to the principle of proportionality.

questions.q: According to the *M. Siddiq (2019)* judgement, who was the deity awarded the disputed land in Ayodhya?
questions.e: The Supreme Court awarded the entire 2.77 acres of disputed land to the deity 'Ram Lalla Virajman'.

questions.q: In which case did the Supreme Court declare that "Secularism is a part of the basic structure of the constitution"?
questions.e: The S.R. Bommai case of 1994 explicitly listed secularism as a core component of the Constitution's basic structure.

questions.q: What was the reason for striking down Section 497 of the IPC in the *Joseph Shine case*?
o: It was not being implemented by the police.
Adultery was not considered a wrong in ancient India.
It violated the rights to equality and non-discrimination.
It allowed women to divorce their husbands too easily.
questions.e: The Court struck down the adultery law because it was discriminatory against women and violated the principles of gender equality under Articles 14 and 15.

questions.q: The 'Right to Privacy' (Puttaswamy case) overturned which of the following earlier judgements?
questions.e: The nine-judge bench in Puttaswamy explicitly overruled the M.P. Sharma (1954) and Kharak Singh (1962) cases, which had previously held that privacy was not a fundamental right.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the 'three-fold requirements' for an invasion of life or personal liberty as per the *K.S. Puttaswamy* judgement?
questions.e: The Court laid down that any invasion of privacy or liberty must meet the tests of legality, need/legitimacy, and proportionality. Consent is not listed as one of these three specific constitutional tests.

questions.q: In the *Lily Thomas case (2013)*, the Supreme Court held that Parliament does not have the power to make different laws for:
o: The Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha.
Disqualification for being chosen as a member and for continuing as a member.
questions.e: The Court ruled that Articles 102 and 191 do not allow for different disqualification standards for prospective candidates and sitting members, thus striking down the 'grace period' for sitting members.

questions.q: The *T.S.R. Subramanian case (2013)* is associated with which set of reforms?
questions.e: This case dealt with the accountability and stability of civil servants, leading to directions for setting up Civil Service Boards and fixed tenures.

questions.q: What did the Supreme Court mandate in the *T.S.R. Subramanian case* regarding instructions given to civil servants?
o: They should be in writing and formally recorded if given orally.
Oral instructions are more important than written ones.
They must always be followed, whether oral or written.
Civil servants should only follow instructions from the Prime Minister.
questions.e: To ensure transparency and accountability, the Court mandated that civil servants should not act on mere verbal instructions and that all orders should be recorded in writing.

questions.q: Which constitutional amendment was upheld (validated) in the *Kesavananda Bharati case (1973)*?
questions.e: While propounding the basic structure doctrine, the Court upheld the 24th Amendment Act, which affirmed Parliament's power to amend any part of the Constitution.

questions.q: The *I.C. Golak Nath case* led to the enactment of which amendment act?
questions.e: The 24th Amendment (1971) was passed as a direct sequel to override the Golak Nath judgement's restriction on Parliament's power to amend Fundamental Rights.

questions.q: Which of the following cases led to the enactment of the *46th Amendment Act (1982)*? 1️⃣ State of Madras vs. M/s. Gannon Dunkerley & Co. 2️⃣ New India Sugar Mills vs. Commissioner of Sales Tax. 3️⃣ Northern India Caterers vs. Lt. Governor of Delhi.
questions.e: Several cases dealing with sales tax and commercial transactions, including Gannon Dunkerley, New India Sugar Mills, and Northern India Caterers, collectively led to the 46th Amendment.

questions.q: The *P.A. Inamdar case (2005)* led to the enactment of which amendment?
questions.e: Following the T.M.A. Pai and Inamdar cases, the 93rd Amendment (2005) was enacted to provide for reservations in private educational institutions.

questions.q: In the *Minerva Mills case*, which clause of Article 368 was declared unconstitutional?
questions.e: Clauses (4) and (5) of Article 368, which attempted to give Parliament unlimited power and exclude judicial review, were struck down as they destroyed the basic structure.

questions.q: The "Right to Reputation" was declared as an integral part of Article 21 in which case?
o: Sheela Barse vs. State of Maharashtra
Board of Trustees of Port of Bombay vs. Dilip Kumar R. Nadkarni
Prem Shankar Shukla vs. Delhi Administration
questions.e: In this 1982 case, the Supreme Court recognized that an individual's reputation is a vital facet of their personal liberty and life under Article 21.

questions.q: Which of the following cases dealt with the 'Right to free legal aid'?
o: M.H. Hoskot vs. State of Maharashtra
Prem Shankar Shukla vs. Delhi Administration
questions.e: In the 1978 Hoskot case, the Court held that the right to free legal aid for the indigent is a fundamental right implicit in Article 21.

questions.q: Regarding the *S.R. Bommai case*, which of the following is NOT true?
o: The assembly can be dissolved as soon as the Governor recommends President's Rule.
Secularism is a basic feature of the Constitution.
The floor of the house is the only place to test the majority of a ministry.
Proclamations under Article 356 are subject to judicial review.
questions.e: The Court specifically ruled that the assembly should not be dissolved before Parliament approves the proclamation; it can only be suspended until then.

questions.q: The "Golden Triangle" of the Indian Constitution refers to the inter-relation between which Articles?
questions.e: Established in the Maneka Gandhi case, the 'golden triangle' rule signifies that Articles 14, 19, and 21 are not mutually exclusive and must be read together.

questions.q: In the *Indra Sawhney case*, the SC invalidated 10% additional reservation for:
o: Economically backward sections not covered by existing schemes
questions.e: While upholding OBC reservations, the Court struck down a separate 10% reservation based solely on economic criteria for the general category at that time.

questions.q: The *Waman Rao case (1980)* is primarily associated with:
o: Declaring the Right to Property as part of the basic structure.
Allowing the Parliament to rewrite the entire Constitution.
Setting April 24, 1973, as the cut-off date for judicial review of the Ninth Schedule.
questions.e: The Court ruled that amendments to the Ninth Schedule made after the Kesavananda Bharati verdict are open to challenge on basic structure grounds.

questions.q: Which case dealt with the 'Right against public hanging'?
o: Parmanand Katara vs. Union of India
T.V. Vatheeswaran vs. State of Tamil Nadu
Attorney General of India vs. Lachma Devi
questions.e: In 1985, the Court held that public hanging is a barbaric practice and violates the right to live with human dignity under Article 21.

questions.q: The "Right to Sleep" was recognized as a fundamental right in the context of:
questions.e: In the 2012 Ramlila Maidan case, the Court recognized that sleep is a biological necessity and the right to sleep is a facet of the right to life.

questions.q: In the *M. Nagaraj case (2006)*, the Supreme Court upheld the validity of which amendment(s)?
questions.e: The Court upheld these amendments which related to reservations in promotions for SCs and STs, provided certain criteria like backwardness and efficiency are maintained.

questions.q: What was the Supreme Court's verdict in the *Bachan Singh case (1980)*?
o: Death penalty is constitutional but should be used in the 'rarest of rare' cases.
Death penalty is mandatory for all murders.
The Governor's power to pardon is abolished.
questions.e: The Court upheld Section 302 IPC but restricted the use of the death penalty to exceptional and grave circumstances.

questions.q: The *Satwant Singh Sawhney case (1967)* established the fundamental right to:
questions.e: This early landmark case established that the right to travel abroad is part of 'personal liberty' under Article 21.

questions.q: Regarding the *Shayara Bano case (2017)*, what form of divorce was specifically banned?
questions.e: The Court specifically struck down Talaq-e-Biddat, which allowed a husband to divorce instantly without any attempt at reconciliation.

questions.q: In the *NALSA case*, the Court linked 'gender identity' to which of the following?
o: The political party of the individual
questions.e: The Court held that gender identity is integral to human dignity and falls under the rights to autonomy and self-determination protected by Article 21.

questions.q: Which case is known as the 'Oleum Gas Leak case'?
o: Indra Sawhney vs. Union of India
M.C. Mehta vs. Union of India
Vineet Narain vs. Union of India
S.R. Bommai vs. Union of India
questions.e: The 1986 case following a gas leak in Delhi led to the landmark principle of absolute liability for hazardous industries.

questions.q: According to the NCRWC, how many children below age 14 were in India at the time of the report?
questions.e: The commission noted with concern that 380 million children were below age 14 and arrangements for their well-being were inadequate.

questions.q: The NCRWC noted that what percentage of the primary education budget goes for salaries alone?
questions.e: Highlighting a major fiscal concern in social infrastructure, the report stated that 96.4% of the primary education budget was consumed by salaries.

questions.q: Which of the following diseases were mentioned by NCRWC as showing an "alarming increase"?
questions.e: The commission raised concern over public health, noting the rise in infectious diseases like TB, Malaria, and HIV.

questions.q: The NCRWC recommended that the *MP local area development scheme* should be:
questions.e: In its recommendations on Parliament and State Legislatures, the commission explicitly suggested the discontinuation of the MP local area development scheme.

questions.q: What did the NCRWC recommend regarding the "Right to Information"?
o: It should be discouraged to maintain secrecy.
It should be guaranteed, and an oath of transparency should replace the oath of secrecy.
It is already fully implemented and needs no changes.
It should only be available to the media.
questions.e: The commission advocated for discarding traditional secrecy in favor of transparency and a guaranteed Right to Information.

questions.q: Regarding the "Hung Parliament", the NCRWC suggested that:
o: The outgoing Prime Minister should continue indefinitely.
A fresh election must be held immediately.
The Lok Sabha may elect the leader of the House to be appointed as Prime Minister.
The President should choose the leader randomly.
questions.e: To handle instability, the commission recommended that the House itself elect a leader if no party has a majority.

questions.q: The NCRWC recommended setting up a "National Immigration Council" primarily to:
o: Encourage more people to leave India.
Build a wall around the country.
Examine issues like a review of the Citizenship Act and Illegal Migrants Determination Act.
questions.e: This was a specific recommendation for institutions in North East India to address migration and citizenship issues.

questions.q: What percentage of valid votes must a candidate poll to avoid forfeiting their deposit, according to NCRWC recommendations?
questions.e: The commission proposed increasing the threshold from the current 16.67% to 25% to discourage non-serious candidates.

questions.q: Which case is popularly known as the "Second Judges case"?
o: Supreme Court Advocates-on-Record Association vs. Union of India (1993)
S.P. Gupta vs. Union of India
questions.e: The 1993 Advocates-on-Record case is known as the Second Judges case, which established the dominance of the judiciary in appointments.

questions.q: In the *Vineet Narain case*, the "Single Directive" (which was struck down) required the CBI to:
o: Report only to the Prime Minister.
Obtain prior permission before investigating officers of Joint Secretary rank and above.
Investigation only one case at a time.
questions.e: The Court struck down this directive as arbitrary, as it protected high-ranking officers from investigation without government permission.

questions.q: According to the *T.M.A. Pai* judgement, a minority institution that receives government aid:
o: Must only teach government-approved religious texts.
Can still refuse admission to other communities.
Must not refuse admission on grounds of religion, race, caste, or language.
questions.e: The Court held that once aid is received, Article 29(2) applies, and the institution cannot give exclusive preference to its own community.

questions.q: The "Right to fly the national flag freely" (Naveen Jindal case) is NOT absolute and cannot be used for:
questions.e: While recognizing it as a fundamental right, the Court clarified it cannot be used for commercial benefit.

questions.q: One of the seven directives in the *Prakash Singh case* was the separation of:
o: The State police from the Central police.
The Investigation police from the Law and Order police.
questions.e: This was a key directive aimed at improving the quality of criminal investigations and preventing interference by law-and-order duties.

questions.q: The *I.R. Coelho case* is often referred to as the:
questions.e: This 2007 case is famous for its definitive ruling on the judicial review of the Ninth Schedule.

questions.q: Under the *Aruna Shanbaug* guidelines, who can take a decision to discontinue life support if the parents or spouse are absent?
o: A person acting as a 'next friend' or the attending doctors.
The decision cannot be taken at all.
questions.e: In the absence of close relatives, the Court allowed a 'next friend' or doctors to initiate the process, subject to High Court approval.

questions.q: The *Lily Thomas case* struck down Section 8(4) of the RPA 1951 as being:
o: Beyond the powers conferred on Parliament (ultra vires).
Only applicable to the Lok Sabha.
Valid but needs more time to implement.
questions.e: The Court found that Section 8(4) created an unconstitutional distinction between sitting members and others.

questions.q: In the *NALSA case*, the Supreme Court directed that transgender persons should be treated as:
o: Socially and educationally backward classes of citizens.
questions.e: This classification allows them to access reservations in education and public appointments.

questions.q: Which section of the IT Act was struck down in the *Shreya Singhal case*?
questions.e: Section 66A was invalidated because its vagueness led to the arbitrary arrest of citizens for online speech.

questions.q: In the *Shayara Bano case*, the Court held that what is held to be "bad in theology" is:
o: Not a concern for the court.
questions.e: The Court used this reasoning to show that since Triple Talaq is considered bad in the Quran, it cannot be legally valid.

questions.q: Which article was the primary basis for the "Right to Privacy" in the *Puttaswamy case*?
questions.e: The Court located privacy as an intrinsic part of the right to life and personal liberty under Article 21.

questions.q: The "Aadhaar judgement" is also known as:
questions.e: This 2018 judgement upheld the Aadhaar Act while striking down certain provisions, following the privacy principles laid down in the first Puttaswamy case.

questions.q: In the *Sabarimala case*, which Rule of the Kerala Hindu Places of Public Worship Rules was struck down?
questions.e: Rule 3(b) was the provision that prohibited the entry of women into the temple.

questions.q: After the *Joseph Shine case*, adultery in India is:
o: Only a crime for men, not women.
A criminal offence with 10 years jail.
No longer a criminal offence but a civil wrong and ground for divorce.
questions.e: The Court decriminalized adultery but noted it remains a valid ground for dissolving a marriage under civil law.

questions.q: The *Navtej Singh Johar* judgement overruled which 2013 case?
questions.e: The 2013 Koushal case had previously overturned a Delhi HC judgement and upheld Section 377; Navtej Johar finally struck it down.

questions.q: In the Ayodhya judgement, the UP Sunni Central Waqf Board was allotted how much alternative land?
questions.e: The Court directed the allotment of 5 acres of land at a prominent place in Ayodhya for the construction of a mosque.

questions.q: The *Anuradha Bhasin case* led to the emergence of which right as a fundamental right?
o: Right to call anyone at any time.
Right to free social media accounts.
Right to access to the internet.
questions.e: The judgement recognized that the internet is an essential medium for exercising constitutional rights.

questions.q: In the *Rambabu Singh Thakur case*, "winnability at the polls" was:
o: Held as the most important reason for selecting a candidate.
Rejected as the sole reason for selecting a candidate with a criminal record.
Made the only legal criteria for candidates.
questions.e: The Court ordered that selection must be based on merit and achievements, not just because a candidate is likely to win.

questions.q: The *Internet and Mobile Association of India case* (2020) removed the ban on:
questions.e: The SC struck down the RBI circular that prevented banks from facilitating virtual currency trades.

questions.q: The "Right to free education up to 14 years of age" was declared as part of Article 21 in which case (1993)?
questions.e: While Mohini Jain said it extends to all levels, Unni Krishnan narrowed it to the 14-year age limit as a mandatory right.

questions.q: Which case is popularly known as the "Mandal case"?
o: Indra Sawhney vs. Union of India
Kesavananda Bharati vs. State of Kerala
S.R. Bommai vs. Union of India
Minerva Mills vs. Union of India
questions.e: This landmark 1992 case dealt with the implementation of the Mandal Commission's recommendations for OBC reservations.

questions.q: The "Right to Speedy Trial" was recognized in:
o: M.H. Hoskot vs. State of Maharashtra
Hussainara Khatoon vs. Home Secretary, Bihar
Prem Shankar Shukla vs. Delhi Administration
questions.e: This 1979 case highlighted the plight of under-trials and established the right to a quick judicial process.

questions.q: Which case is associated with the "Right against public hanging"?
o: Bachan Singh vs. State of Punjab
Attorney General of India vs. Lachma Devi
questions.e: The Supreme Court held that public hanging is unconstitutional and violates Article 21.

questions.q: The *Champakam Dorairajan case* (1951) was related to:
o: The abolition of the Zamindari system.
questions.e: This case led to the first constitutional amendment to allow reservations for backward classes.

questions.q: In the *Romesh Thappar case* (1950), the Madras government had banned a weekly journal called:
questions.e: The journal 'Cross Roads' was published in Bombay, and its ban by Madras was declared void.

questions.q: Which case is popularly known as the "Fundamental Rights case"?
questions.e: The Kesavananda Bharati case is so named because of its massive impact on the status of Fundamental Rights versus Parliament's amending power.

questions.q: The *Berubari Union case* involved the implementation of an agreement between:
questions.e: The agreement, known as the Nehru-Noon Agreement, related to the exchange of enclaves.

questions.q: "Victimology and victim-protection" were mentioned as areas of concern by the:
questions.e: The NCRWC highlighted the lack of institutional arrangements for protecting witnesses and victims in sensitive trials.

questions.q: The NCRWC recommended that the domicile requirement for contesting elections to the Rajya Sabha should be:
o: Maintained to ensure the federal character.
Changed to only include property owners.
questions.e: The commission felt that Rajya Sabha members should genuinely represent the state from which they are elected.

questions.q: Which of the following bodies did the NCRWC recommend should be set up to promote inter-religious harmony?
questions.e: This was a recommendation under the Directive Principles to foster social solidarity.

questions.q: The NCRWC recommended that "Black-money and parallel economy" should be:
o: Made legal to collect more taxes.
questions.e: The commission warned that failure to confront these realities would allow illegal outfits to dictate terms to the government.

questions.q: Regarding "Communal Riots", the NCRWC stated they should be treated as:
o: Merely a law and order problem.
Problems that resolve themselves over time.
questions.e: The commission emphasized that legal and administrative measures are needed to remove the insecurity felt by minorities.

questions.q: How many recommendations of the NCRWC could be accomplished through *executive action*?
questions.e: The commission provided a breakdown of its 249 recommendations, with 105 being feasible through government orders without new laws or amendments.

questions.q: Which new fundamental right did NCRWC propose for children?
o: Right to own a mobile phone.
Right to care, assistance, and protection.
questions.e: This was recommended to be added to Part III of the Constitution.

questions.q: The NCRWC recommended that the term "Hindu" in Article 25 should no longer include:
questions.e: The commission wanted these religions to be explicitly recognized as separate groups.

questions.q: "Arakshan Nyaya Adalats" were recommended by NCRWC to:
questions.e: This was part of the recommendations on the pace of socio-economic change for weaker sections.

questions.q: The NCRWC suggested that the *Chief Election Commissioner* should be appointed by a committee including:
o: The Chief Justice of India only.
PM, Leaders of Opposition in both houses, Speaker, and Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha.
questions.e: This was proposed to ensure the independence and non-partisan nature of the Election Commission.

questions.q: According to NCRWC, a political party should be deregistered if it:
o: Provides a ticket to a candidate with framed criminal charges or a conviction.
questions.e: This was a strict recommendation to clean up the political system.

questions.q: In the *A.K. Gopalan* case, the Court held that 'law' in Article 21 means:
questions.e: The Court adopted a textualist approach, excluding the broader 'due process' or natural justice interpretations.

questions.q: The *Shankari Prasad case* upheld the validity of which amendment?
questions.e: The 1st Amendment had curtailed the right to property by inserting Articles 31A and 31B, which the Court held valid.

questions.q: Which case affirmed that "The Preamble is NOT a part of the Constitution"?
questions.e: This was later overruled in the Kesavananda Bharati case, which held the Preamble IS a part of the Constitution.

questions.q: The *K.M. Nanavati case* involved the murder of the paramour of Nanavati's:
questions.e: Nanavati, a Naval Commander, was tried for the murder of Prem Ahuja.

questions.q: The "Doctrine of Prospective Overruling" was applied in which case?
questions.e: The Court ruled that its decision would only apply to future amendments and not invalidate past ones like the 1st or 17th.

questions.q: Article 329A (Clause 4), which was struck down in the *Indira Gandhi* case, was inserted by the:
questions.e: The 39th Amendment attempted to place the PM's election beyond judicial scrutiny.

questions.q: The 44th Amendment Act (1978) amended Article 359 to ensure that which right(s) cannot be suspended even during an emergency?
questions.e: This was a direct response to the "flawed" A.D.M. Jabalpur judgement during the 1975-77 Emergency.

questions.q: In the *Maneka Gandhi case*, the Court struck down which section of the Passport Act (1967)?
questions.e: While it laid down broad principles, it specifically scrutinized the section used to impound Maneka Gandhi's passport.

questions.q: The "Golden Triangle" rule involves the inter-relation of which three articles?
questions.e: This rule ensures that any law affecting liberty must pass the test of all three fundamental articles.

questions.q: In the *Bachan Singh* case, the Court held that Article 19(1) does not:
o: Protect the freedom of the press.
Guarantee the activity of committing a murder.
questions.e: This was part of the reasoning used to uphold the constitutionality of the death penalty for murder.

questions.q: The *Waman Rao case* fixed which specific date as the cut-off for Ninth Schedule immunity?
questions.e: This is the date the Kesavananda Bharati verdict was delivered, marking the birth of the Basic Structure doctrine.

questions.q: The *Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Divorce) Act, 1986* was enacted to:
o: Give women more rights than the SC provided.
questions.e: The Act restricted the husband's liability to pay maintenance only to the iddat period, reversing the SC's broader ruling.

questions.q: In the *D.C. Wadhwa case*, the Governor of Bihar had promulgated how many ordinances between 1967-1981?
questions.e: The Court used this extreme example to highlight the systematic misuse of ordinance powers.

questions.q: The "Oleum Gas Leak case" occurred at the Shriram Food and Fertilizers plant in:
questions.e: The 1986 leak led to M.C. Mehta's landmark case on industrial liability.

questions.q: In the *Kihoto Hollohan case*, the SC struck down Paragraph 7 of the Tenth Schedule because it:
o: Excluded the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court and High Courts.
questions.e: The Court held that taking away judicial review required ratification by state legislatures.

questions.q: The *Indra Sawhney* case mandated the appointment of which committee to identify the 'creamy layer'?
questions.e: This was part of the impact of the judgement to ensure reservation benefits reach the truly backward.

questions.q: "Capitation Fee" was described as "nothing but a price for selling education" in which case?
questions.e: The Court in Mohini Jain ruled that charging such fees violates the right to equality and education.

questions.q: The *Unni Krishnan case* (1993) held that the Right to Education is a fundamental right but narrowed it to:
o: Only those who can afford it.
Children of the age of six to fourteen years.
questions.e: This later became the basis for the 86th Amendment.

questions.q: Which amendment added Article 21A to the Constitution?
questions.e: Enacted in 2002, this amendment made free and compulsory education for children 6-14 a fundamental right.

questions.q: The *S.R. Bommai* judgement placed a check on the arbitrary use of which article?
questions.e: This case is the primary legal check on the imposition of President's Rule in states.

questions.q: In the *Vishaka case*, the Court noted that until suitable legislation is enacted:
o: The Court's guidelines must be strictly observed.
Only the police can decide the rules.
Sexual harassment is not a crime.
questions.e: These 'Vishaka Guidelines' filled a legislative vacuum for 16 years.

questions.q: The *Vineet Narain* judgement led to the enactment of which 2003 Act?
questions.e: The CVC Act of 2003 conferred statutory status upon the Central Vigilance Commission as directed by the SC.

questions.q: In the *Poll Reforms case (2002)*, information about the candidate must be furnished at the time of:
questions.e: This ensures that voters have the necessary information before the election process begins.

questions.q: Which case established that for linguistic and religious minorities, the "unit" is the State?
questions.e: This prevents a group that is a majority in a state from claiming minority benefits based on national population.

questions.q: The *Prakash Singh case* (2006) issued how many specific directives for police reforms?
questions.e: These directives included the creation of a State Security Commission and fixed tenures for police chiefs.

questions.q: The *M. Nagaraj* case dealt with reservation in:
questions.e: The Court upheld the constitutional validity of several amendments allowing for such reservations.

questions.q: "Passive Euthanasia" refers to:
o: A practice that is completely legal without any conditions.
Withdrawing life support or medical treatment.
Killing a person without their consent.
questions.e: The Aruna Shanbaug case established the legal framework for this in India.

questions.q: The "None of the Above" (NOTA) button was first provided in general elections in which year?
questions.e: Following the 2013 PUCL judgement, it was first used in state elections and then the 2014 Lok Sabha elections.

questions.q: Which section of the RPA 1951 was struck down in the *Lily Thomas case*?
questions.e: This section previously allowed convicted MPs/MLAs to continue in office pending appeal.

questions.q: The *NALSA case* recognized transgender persons' right to decide:
o: Who should be the Prime Minister.
questions.e: This includes legal recognition as male, female, or third gender.

questions.q: The *Fourth Judges case* (2015) restored which system of judicial appointments?
questions.e: By striking down the NJAC, the Court revived the system established in the Second and Third Judges cases.

questions.q: The "Triple Talaq Act" was passed in:
questions.e: Formally known as the Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act, it was a sequel to the Shayara Bano judgement.

questions.q: In the *Puttaswamy case*, the Court ruled that the Right to Privacy is:
o: Not an absolute right and subject to reasonable restrictions.
questions.e: Like other fundamental rights, privacy is subject to restrictions placed in the interest of the state or public order.

questions.q: The *Sabarimala case* involved women of which age group?
o: Women of the age group 10-50 years.
questions.e: The ban was specifically on women of menstruating age.

questions.q: Adultery was previously a criminal offence under which section of the IPC?
questions.e: This section was struck down in the Joseph Shine case as being unconstitutional.

questions.q: Homosexuality was decriminalized by partly striking down:
questions.e: The Navtej Singh Johar case held that consensual acts between adults are not criminal.

questions.q: The *Ayodhya judgement* (2019) was delivered by a bench of how many judges?
questions.e: (Contextual knowledge of M. Siddiq case) The 2019 verdict was a unanimous decision by a five-judge Constitution Bench.

questions.q: "NOTA" stands for:
questions.e: It allows voters to reject all candidates in a constituency.

questions.q: Which case is associated with the "Right to Sleep"?
questions.e: The SC recognized sleep as a fundamental facet of Article 21.

questions.q: The "Right to Information" was explicitly linked to which article by NCRWC?
questions.e: The commission viewed it as an essential part of the freedom of speech and expression.

questions.q: The *M. Siddiq case* put an end to a dispute that was:
questions.e: The legal dispute over the Ayodhya site had been ongoing in various forms since the 19th century.

questions.q: According to the *Anuradha Bhasin* judgement, any order suspending internet must adhere to:
o: The religious beliefs of the area.
The wishes of the local police chief only.
questions.e: Proportionality ensures the restriction is not more than necessary to achieve its aim.

questions.q: Political parties must publish the criminal antecedents of candidates in:
o: One local vernacular newspaper and one national newspaper.
They do not need to publish them.
questions.e: This was a directive from the Rambabu Singh Thakur case to ensure wide publicity.

questions.q: The *Internet and Mobile Association of India* case involved which regulatory body?
questions.e: The case was a challenge to a circular issued by the Reserve Bank of India regarding virtual currencies.

questions.q: Which case declared the "Right against solitary confinement"?
o: Bachan Singh vs. State of Punjab
Prem Shankar Shukla vs. Delhi Administration
questions.e: The Court held that solitary confinement is a harsh punishment that affects the right to life.

questions.q: The "Right to decent environment" was recognized in:
o: Dr. B.L. Wadhera vs. Union of India
M.C. Mehta vs. Union of India
Vellore Citizens Welfare Forum vs. Union of India
Rural Litigation and Entitlement Kendra vs. State of U.P.
questions.e: Also known as the Dehradun Quarrying case, it was a landmark for environmental rights in 1985.

questions.q: The "Right to Health" was recognized in:
o: Consumer Education and Research Centre vs. Union of India
Unni Krishnan vs. State of A.P.
Mohini Jain vs. State of Karnataka
questions.e: The SC held that the right to health is a fundamental right of workers and citizens under Article 21.

questions.q: Which case established the "Right not to be driven out of a state"?
o: NHRC vs. State of Arunachal Pradesh (Chakmas Migrants case)
S.R. Bommai vs. Union of India
Mohini Jain vs. State of Karnataka
questions.e: The Court protected the rights of Chakma refugees against arbitrary expulsion.

questions.q: The "Right to Social and Economic Justice" was declared as part of Article 21 in:
o: Indra Sawhney vs. Union of India
Ashok Kumar Gupta vs. State of U.P.
M. Nagaraj vs. Union of India
Unni Krishnan vs. State of A.P.
questions.e: This 1997 judgement linked socio-economic empowerment to the fundamental right to life.

questions.q: The *Lily Thomas case* struck down Section 8(4) of the RPA 1951. This section was:
o: About the symbol of political parties.
A 'saving' clause for sitting members from immediate disqualification.
questions.e: Its removal ended the special protection sitting legislators had upon conviction.

questions.q: The *Vineet Narain* judgement aimed at making the CBI:
o: A part of the Ministry of Home Affairs.
An autonomous body and non-partisan agency.
questions.e: The goal was to ensure efficient and independent functioning of investigative agencies.

questions.q: According to the *Association for Democratic Reforms* case, "Democracy cannot survive without":
questions.e: Informed voters are the bedrock of a functioning democratic system.

questions.q: In the *T.M.A. Pai* case, the Court held that the right to establish educational institutions:
o: Is not available to religious minorities.
Is absolute and cannot be restricted.
Includes professional educational institutions like medicine and engineering.
questions.e: The words "of their choice" in Article 30 were interpreted broadly.

questions.q: The NCRWC identified how many areas of study on its own?
questions.e: These eleven areas formed the core of the commission's extensive review.

questions.q: The *Indra Sawhney* judgement (1992) upheld reservation for OBCs in:
questions.e: The Court specifically ruled out reservation in promotions at that time.

questions.q: Which case dealt with the "Right to compensation" for illegal deprivation of life or liberty?
questions.e: The M.C. Mehta Oleum Gas case expanded the power of the SC under Article 32 to award such compensation.

questions.q: The "system of trial by jury" was completely removed in India by:
questions.e: This followed the impact of the K.M. Nanavati case which showed the system's flaws.

questions.q: The *Sajjan Singh case* (1964) re-affirmed the judgement of:
questions.e: It upheld the Parliament's power to amend any part of the Constitution before the Golak Nath reversal.

questions.q: Which amendment gave effect to the transfer of *Berubari Union* to Pakistan?
questions.e: This amendment was necessary after the SC ruled that Article 3 could not be used for ceding territory.

questions.q: The *A.D.M. Jabalpur* case argued that any claim to a writ of habeas corpus:
o: Should only be heard after the emergency.
Was a fundamental right of every human.
Amounted to the enforcement of the right to life, which was suspended.
questions.e: This restrictive reasoning led to a judgement that is now considered "seriously flawed".

questions.q: In the *Maneka Gandhi case*, the Court held that Article 21 is a protection against:
o: Both the Executive and arbitrary Legislative action.
questions.e: This marked a major shift from the A.K. Gopalan interpretation.

questions.q: "Self-determination of gender" is at the core of:
questions.e: The NALSA judgement identified this as a vital facet of human dignity under Article 21.

questions.q: In the *Shreya Singhal* case, Section 66A was found to be:
questions.e: Its broad nature allowed it to be used to suppress legitimate speech.

questions.q: The *Fourth Judges case* (2015) declared the 99th Amendment void because it affected:
o: The power of the Prime Minister.
questions.e: Judicial independence is a recognized component of the Constitution's basic structure.

questions.q: In the *Shayara Bano* case, the Court held that triple talaq is against the basic tenets of:
questions.e: The Court found that what is theologically bad cannot be legally good.

questions.q: Which case influence the *Indian Young Lawyers Association* (Sabarimala) and *Joseph Shine* (Adultery) cases?
questions.e: The broad interpretation of individual autonomy and rights in the privacy case set the stage for these later judgements.

questions.q: "Aadhaar law" was upheld by the SC in 2018 but it:
o: Made Aadhaar mandatory for all private transactions.
Ordered the destruction of all biometric data.
Struck down certain provisions and suggested changes.
questions.e: This led to the Aadhaar and Other Laws (Amendment) Act, 2019.

questions.q: The *Sabarimala Review Bench* in 2019 referred the case to:
o: The Prime Minister for a decision.
questions.e: This indicates the complexity and ongoing nature of the legal issues involved.

questions.q: After adultery was decriminalized, it can still be considered a:
o: Civil wrong and ground for dissolution of marriage.
Reason to lose the right to vote.
questions.e: While no longer a crime, it remains a serious issue in family law.

questions.q: Consensual sexual acts of adults of the same sex were decriminalized in which year?
questions.e: This was the result of the landmark Navtej Singh Johar judgement.

questions.q: The Ayodhya verdict directed that the trust for the Ram Mandir should give representation to:
questions.e: This was to acknowledge the Akhara's long-standing role in the site.

questions.q: "None of the Above" (NOTA) ensures that a voter can maintain:
questions.e: It protects the identity of those who choose not to support any candidate.

questions.q: The NCRWC report consists of how many volumes mentioned in the text?
questions.e: Footnotes refer to Volume 1, Chapters 1, 2, 3, 10, and 11.

questions.q: Which former Speaker of the Lok Sabha was a member of the NCRWC?
questions.e: Sangma served as a member until his resignation shortly before the report was submitted.

questions.q: The NCRWC was tasked to review the working of the Constitution in the light of the experience of the past:
questions.e: The commission looked at the five decades since the Constitution's adoption in 1950.

questions.q: "Rural de-population and urbanization" were identified as concerns by NCRWC because they:
o: Need immediate attention and solutions to prevent social unrest.
Should be encouraged by the government.
questions.e: The commission saw these as threats to an orderly government and stable society.

questions.q: The "Right to suitable rehabilitation" was recommended specifically for:
o: SCs and STs if their land is acquired.
questions.e: This was a recommendation to recast Article 300-A.

questions.q: The NCRWC recommended that the minimum number of days for sittings of the *Lok Sabha* should be fixed at:
questions.e: It suggested 100 days for Rajya Sabha and 120 days for Lok Sabha to ensure better accountability.

questions.q: A "system of constructive vote of no confidence" is used in which country according to common political science (and implied by the term)?
o: Germany (Contextual knowledge, though NCRWC simply proposes it for India)
questions.e: The NCRWC recommended this system, where an alternative leader must be named, to bring stability to the Executive.

questions.q: The NCRWC recommended that the *Prime Minister* should be:
o: The person who appoints the Lokpal alone.
Kept outside the purview of Lokpal.
Included in the purview of Lokpal.
questions.e: This was a specific recommendation regarding the office of Lokpal.

questions.q: "Lateral entry" into government jobs was recommended by NCRWC for levels:
questions.e: This was proposed to bring in specialized expertise from outside the traditional civil service.

questions.q: The NCRWC recommended that "Disaster Management" should be included in:
o: It should not be in any list.
questions.e: This would allow both the Centre and States to make laws on the subject.

questions.q: A "National Judicial Commission" was recommended to comprise how many senior most Judges of the Supreme Court?
questions.e: The proposed commission included the CJI, two senior judges, the Law Minister, and a nominee of the President.

questions.q: "Plea-bargaining" was recommended by NCRWC as part of:
questions.e: This was a recommendation for the judiciary to reduce the backlog of cases.

questions.q: The "Citizens' Charters" were recommended to be prepared by:
questions.e: This was intended to enumerate the entitlements of citizens, especially deprived classes.

questions.q: The "Employment of Manual Scavengers Act, 1993" should be:
questions.e: This was part of the NCRWC's recommendations on the pace of socio-economic change.

questions.q: The "CAG of India" should be empowered to conduct the audit of:
o: Only the Prime Minister's personal accounts.
questions.e: The NCRWC recommended this to ensure uniformity in accounting standards for local bodies.

questions.q: A "Delimitation Commission" was recommended to handle:
o: The reservation and rotation of seats in local bodies.
questions.e: This function was proposed to be taken away from the State Election Commission.

questions.q: "State funding of elections" according to NCRWC should be:
o: Deferred until regulatory mechanisms for political parties are in position.
questions.e: The commission felt that political parties must first be regulated by law.

questions.q: The *Justice Verma Committee* (1998) was appointed to:
o: Select the Chief Justice of India.
Operationalise the suggestions to teach Fundamental Duties.
questions.e: The NCRWC recommended the early implementation of this committee's report.

questions.q: How many members were in the National Commission to Review the Working of the Constitution?
questions.e: The commission was an 11-member body chaired by M.N. Venkatachaliah.
